title: Moving money between owner and business

sections.skill: Record contributions, draws and owner loans correctly

questions.prompt: Money an owner puts into the business is called what?

choices.text: An owner's draw for personal use
A customer payment for a product

questions.intro: Owners move money in and out of a business in a few ways. An OWNER CONTRIBUTION is money the owner puts in. An OWNER'S DRAW (also called a distribution) is an owner withdrawal for personal use; for sole proprietors and most LLCs, a draw is not a wage and is not a business expense, so it lowers the business's cash but does not reduce its profit. A LOAN from the owner to the business should be written down with how it will be repaid. In every case, move the money by transfer and record what it is, so the books show the truth.
questions.feedback: A contribution is money in from the owner.

sections.skill: A family piggy bank with a notebook

choices.text: A refund paid to a customer

questions.intro: Picture a family piggy bank with a notebook next to it. When you put money in, you write "Added 50." When you take money out, you write "Took 20." If you borrow from it, you write "Borrowed 30, will repay Friday." The notebook tells the true story. Owner contributions, draws and loans are the same idea: money moves in and out, and each move is written down.
